title: Micro-sprint Catalyst — 3-minute feature blueprint journal
body:
Context / intent:
This is a lightweight personal notebook for the idea: "micro-sprint catalyst" — a repeatable blueprint to design, implement and measure a tiny product experiment in ~3 minutes of engineer time (plus a code toggle). The goal is shipping many tiny, reversible features that explore UX, cost signals and routing policy heuristics without heavy PRD overhead.

Why this feels useful:
- We have lots of half-baked instincts about small routing/response tweaks that could move the needle on cost/latency.
- Current experiment ops require too many meetings and infra changes.
- If we can create a templated onramp (API + toggle + telemetry + rollback) teams will try 5x more ideas.

Hypothesis:
If we provide a single-API blueprint with a one-line feature toggle, pre-wired telemetry, and a minimal SDK helper, teams will run fast experiments and we’ll surface clear signals for model/route changes — increasing learning velocity and helping Optimize recommend better profiles.

Success metrics (initial):
- # micro-sprints launched per week (target 8 across org)
- median time from idea -> measurable traffic (target < 1 day)
- percent of micro-sprints that produce a clear signal (delta on cost/latency or quality) within 2 weeks (target 30%)
- rollback rate (target < 10%)

Core blueprint (what ships):
1) Minimal feature toggle config: name, route, constraint (e.g., % traffic, user segment), fallback route
2) SDK helper: enableFeature('micro-catalyst', {pct:10, seed:1234}) returns decorated request context
3) Telemetry contract: emit event micro_sprint.experiment_{start,decision,outcome} with fields {experiment_id, route, model, tokens, latency_ms, cost_usd_est, user_segment}
4) Rollback helper: CLI flag to disable experiment across regions in one step
5) Lightweight doc template that captures hypothesis + acceptance criteria + stop conditions

User stories (examples):
- As a product engineer I want to try a token-pruning policy for casual users on a low-traffic route so I can measure 10% cost reduction without degrading NPS
- As an SRE I want an automated way to drain traffic from an experiment if 95th percentile latency climbs > 2x baseline for 5 minutes
- As a data analyst I want consistent telemetry fields so I can slice experiments by customer tier and model variant quickly

Acceptance criteria (for first template):
- Toggle flips on/off for route via a single SDK call and a central feature flag (no infra deploy)
- Telemetry shows up in BI within 10 minutes of activation with the agreed schema
- Canary support: rollout to X% traffic, per-region limits enforced
- Safety: auto-kill when latency/cost/quality threshold breached (configurable)

Engineering constraints / notes:
- Keep runtime changes minimal: prefer route-level middleware that inspects request context, not model binaries
- Use existing routing/fallback mechanism (no new routing stack) — wire into smart routing policy layer
- Telemetry events should be small and batched; reuse existing event bus topic micro-experiments-v1
- Provide sample implementation for hosted-api SDK and an example for Dedicated customers (how they can mirror toggle via API)

Quick proto API sketch (pseudo):
- POST /v1/experiments - create experiment (name, target_route, pct, stop_conditions)
- PATCH /v1/experiments/:id - update pct/stop_conditions
- POST /v1/experiments/:id/trigger - force evaluate for request (test harness)
- SDK: redwood.experiments.activate('exp-2026-01', {pct:5}) that returns {variant:'control'|'treatment', meta:{exp_id}}

Telemetry contract (example fields):
- event: micro_experiment.invoked
- fields: experiment_id, exp_name, request_id, timestamp, user_tier, route, model, variant, tokens_requested, tokens_used, latency_ms, cost_est_usd, outcome_hint

Experiment lifecycle and measurement plan:
- Day 0: create experiment from template, add hypothesis & acceptance in doc, set pct=1 for smoke for 1 hour
- Day 0–1: expand to 5–10% if no safety triggers
- Day 2–7: collect sufficient samples — run automated A/B analysis for latency and cost; manual eval on quality for 200 seeded prompts
- Stop conditions: auto-stop on latency spike, auto-stop on cost delta > X% vs baseline, or manual stop after negative quality review

Go-to-market / adoption plan (internal):
- Seed with 2 product teams (hosted-api messaging & enrichments) for first month
- Weekly office-hours slot to help teams stand up first micro-sprint (15 min)
- Create a short video (2–3 minutes) demoing toggle + telemetry + rollback

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: noisy telemetry leads to false positives —> Mitigate: require min sample size and use smoothed percentiles
- Risk: teams misuse micro-sprints for large-scope changes —> Mitigate: enforce quota (max duration, max pct), approval gate for >20%
- Risk: feature toggles create statefulness confusion —> Mitigate: one-click global rollback and TTL on experiment configs

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who owns the experiment registry? product infra or platform? (ask @Noor)
- Should there be templated quality evalkits per experiment type (e.g., prompt set for routing, hallucination set for model swap)?
- Define cost_est_usd computation: token pricing vs route-weighting — prototype a quick estimator (Ethan volunteered to sketch)
- UX: add ‘quick-preview’ mode in Console to see prospective cost/latency impact before enabling

Immediate next steps (for me):
- Draft a minimal console mock for 'create micro-sprint' (screenshot + flow) — due 2025-11-10
- Wire telemetry schema into event team (submit schema PR) — due 2025-11-07
- Implement SDK helper stub and example repo with README + toggle example — due 2025-11-21

Notes to self (random):
- Keep template intentionally opinionated: allow only % rollouts, small TTL, and stop-conditions baked in
- Think about building a ‘micro-sprint marketplace’ later where teams can copy published recipes
- This should live in repo: prototyper/micro-sprints (link above PR is prototype)

Scratch ideas (one-liners to iterate later):
- Auto-suggest stop_conditions based on baseline volatility
- Pre-made evaluation packs: cost-only, latency-sensitive, user-experience (human eval quicklist)
- CLI: redwood ms create --template=token-prune --pct=5 --ttl=72h

End of page — rough, but actionable. Revisit after first two seeds.
